newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee nuclear plant sale fails, may shut.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee nuclear plant sale fails, may shut.

text.p: Efforts to sell the Maine Yankee nuclear plant have failed and the board will vote next week on a permanent shutdown for the troubled facility, officials said Friday.
Maine Yankee's board had been in discussions with PECO Energy Co but were unable to reach an agreement, said David Flanagan president of Central Maine Power Co, Maine Yankee's lead owneer.
"This was a good faith effort by PECO Energy and Maine Yankee to find the ecnomic common ground that would benefit both parties," Flanagan said in a prepared statement.

Flanagan said Maine Yankee's board concluded Friday that it could not operate the 810-megawatt plant economically. Officials will "immediately take the regulatory steps necessary to launch decommission," Flanagan said.

The facility has been off-line since December due to design problems in cables of key safety systems. The shutdown was one of a series the plant has suffered since early 1995 due to equipment and safety concerns. Maine Yankee's current utility owners decided in May to suspend repair activities while they looked for a buyer. The owners said the facility would likely be shut down permanently if no buyer were found by early fall.
A Maine Yankee spokeswoman, citing a confidentiality agreement, declined to say why the talks with PECO failed.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
